What does "grounding" mean for an Agentforce agent?
Restricting it to a single Salesforce org
Supplying it with retrieved org data so its answers refer to real records
Disabling its ability to take actions
Running it on Hyperforce rather than a pod
Grounding supplies retrieved context — records, knowledge articles, Data Cloud segments — so the answer is about the customer in front of you rather than a plausible invention.
What is the Einstein Trust Layer?
Protections around generative AI requests, such as data masking, zero data retention with model providers and toxicity detection
A sharing setting for AI-generated records
The Trust Layer sits between the org and the model: it grounds and masks the prompt, checks the response for toxicity and keeps an audit trail.
Under the Trust Layer’s zero data retention, what happens to a prompt sent to a third-party model provider?
The provider neither stores it nor uses it to train its models
It is stored for 30 days for quality review
It is used to train a model for your org only
It is published to the AppExchange
Zero data retention is a contractual commitment with the model providers: prompts and responses are not kept or used for training once the response is returned.
Why does the Trust Layer mask sensitive data before a prompt leaves Salesforce?
So the model sees placeholders instead of the data, which is restored in the response
To stop users reading their own records
Detected personal data is replaced by placeholders before the call and put back when the response returns, so the model never receives it.
What does toxicity detection in the Trust Layer check?
Prompts and responses for harmful or inappropriate content
Content is scored for categories such as hate, violence and profanity, and the scores are recorded with the audit data.
Where are the generative AI audit and feedback records kept?
Prompts, masked data, responses, toxicity scores and user feedback are stored in Data Cloud, where they can be reported on.
In Agentforce, what is a topic?
A category of jobs the agent can do, with its instructions and the actions allowed for it
A Chatter group the agent posts in
A field on the conversation record
Topics scope the agent: a request is classified into a topic, and only that topic’s instructions and actions are in play.
Something the agent can do — run a flow, Apex, a prompt template or an API call
A button on the record page
A user’s reply in the conversation
Actions are the agent’s abilities. Each is built from something the platform already runs, which is why its permissions still apply.
Natural-language guidance on how the agent should behave and decide within that topic
The order of the topic’s screens
Instructions guide reasoning (“always confirm the order number before…”). They influence the model; hard limits come from which actions and permissions it has.
What does the Atlas Reasoning Engine do in Agentforce?
Plans which topic and actions to use for a request, and evaluates the results
The reasoning engine classifies the request, chooses actions, runs them and decides whether more steps are needed before answering.
Reusable prompt templates grounded with merge fields and data
Training data for a custom model
A prompt template combines instructions with merge fields, related lists, flows or Apex, so the same well-tested prompt is used every time.
A customer-facing service agent runs as what?
A dedicated agent user, whose permissions bound what it can see and do
The agent user’s profile and permission sets decide what records and actions the agent can reach, so grant it the minimum.
What is the most reliable way to make sure an agent can never issue a refund?
Do not give it an action that can issue one
Tell it in the instructions never to refund
Add the word “never” to the topic name
Instructions are guidance a model can misread; an action it does not have is a hard limit. Constrain what it can do, then describe how it should do it.
Why test an agent with many differently worded requests before it goes live?
Its responses vary, so you check the right topic and action are chosen across phrasings
Each test request increases its licence count
It only learns from test requests
Language models are probabilistic. Batch testing many utterances shows whether routing and actions hold up, not just whether one demo worked.
What is a hallucination in generative AI?
A fluent answer that is not supported by facts or the data provided
A response that takes too long
An answer in the wrong language
The model produces something plausible rather than something true. Grounding and narrow, checkable tasks reduce it; nothing removes it entirely.
Retrieving relevant content first and passing it to the model with the prompt
Retraining the model on your data every night
Generating several answers and picking the longest
RAG answers from retrieved sources, so the model works from your knowledge base rather than from memory — and can cite what it used.
In Data Cloud-grounded AI, what does a retriever do?
Fetches the most relevant chunks from a search index for a prompt
A retriever queries a search index (vector, keyword or hybrid) and returns the passages that ground the prompt.
Before documents can be searched for grounding, what happens to them?
They are split into chunks and embedded into a search index
They are converted to records on a custom object
They are compressed into a single file
Chunking keeps each passage small enough to be relevant; embeddings turn each chunk into a vector so it can be found by meaning.
Why does semantic search use vector embeddings?
To match by meaning rather than by exact keywords
“Cancel my plan” and “end my subscription” share almost no words but sit close together as vectors, so both find the same article.
Lowering a model’s temperature generally makes its output what?
Low temperature favours the most likely next words, which suits extraction and classification; higher temperature varies the wording more.
Text in user input or retrieved data that tries to override the system’s instructions
Adding merge fields to a template
A faster way to call the model
Inserting a prompt into a flow
“Ignore your instructions and…” hidden in a case description is an attack on the agent. Treat retrieved and user text as data, and bound the agent’s actions.
Why keep a person reviewing an AI-drafted email before it goes to a customer?
Someone checks the facts and tone, and takes responsibility for what is sent
The model cannot write emails without approval
It is required to save the record
It makes the model learn faster
A draft is only a draft. What reaches a customer should be something a person read and put their name to.
What is a large language model?
A model trained on large amounts of text to predict the next token
A rules engine written by admins
It generates text one token at a time from patterns learned in training — which is why fluent output is not the same as correct output.
In a language model, what is a token?
A piece of text, such as a word or part of a word, that the model processes
Limits and costs are counted in tokens, so the same text can cost more in one language than another.
What is a model's context window?
The time it takes to answer
The browser window it runs in
The number of users it serves
The most text, in tokens, it can take into account at once — prompt and response together
Anything outside the window is invisible to the model, which is why grounding retrieves only the relevant passages.
Including a few worked examples in the prompt
Limiting the answer to a few words
Examples show the format and judgement wanted far more reliably than describing them.
Standing instructions that set the model's role and rules for the conversation
A prompt written by the model
It frames every exchange; user text arrives after it and should be treated as data, not as new rules.
Which of these is predictive rather than generative AI?
Scoring how likely a lead is to convert
Drafting a reply to a customer
Predictive models output a score or class from historical data; generative models produce new content.
A model is trained on years of past decisions. What risk does that carry?
It can repeat the biases in those decisions
A model learns what happened, not what should have happened; check outcomes across groups before trusting it.
Why does data quality matter for a grounded agent?
Poor data makes the model faster
The agent's answers can only be as accurate as the records it retrieves
An agent grounded in a stale address will confidently give a stale address.
Which Prompt Builder template type generates text into a field on a record?
A Field Generation template is attached to a field so a user can generate its content from the record in place.
What is a Flex prompt template?
A template with inputs you define, for use cases the other types do not cover
A template that runs without a model
Flex templates take up to several defined inputs, such as records, and can be called from flows, Apex or agents.
How can a flow use a prompt template?
By pasting the prompt into a formula
Through a prompt template action in the flow
The action sends the resolved prompt through the Trust Layer and returns the response to the flow.
A prompt needs data that takes logic to gather. How can the template include it?
Type the data into the template
Ask the user to paste it
Ground it with a flow or Apex that returns the text
A template can call a flow or Apex resource, so the gathering logic is code you can test, not something the model guesses.
Where can a customer-facing Agentforce agent be deployed?
On channels such as Messaging for In-App and Web
The agent is connected to a messaging channel, and conversations can be routed to people through Omni-Channel.
A customer's request is beyond what the agent can do. What is the good design?
Hand the conversation to a person, with its context, through Omni-Channel
Keep answering until the customer gives up
End the conversation without a word
Escalation with the transcript means the customer does not have to start again.
Why do an agent action's input and output descriptions matter?
They set the action's API limits
They are only documentation for admins
The reasoning engine reads them to decide when and how to use the action
Vague descriptions lead to the wrong action or the wrong inputs; write them for the model as carefully as for a colleague.
What does a topic's classification description do?
Helps the reasoning engine decide which requests belong to that topic
Clear, distinct descriptions stop two topics competing for the same request.
What does a topic's scope define?
What the agent may and may not do within that topic
The time zone of the agent
The users who can edit the topic
A precise scope, such as "answers order status questions; does not change orders", keeps the agent within its job.
Why keep the number of actions in a topic small?
Many similar actions make it harder for the reasoning engine to choose the right one
Fewer, clearly different actions make the agent's choices more predictable.
A step must happen in exactly the same way every time. Where should it live?
In a flow or Apex action, not only in the topic's instructions
Instructions guide a probabilistic model; a flow does the same thing every time.
For an action that changes data, what is a sensible instruction?
Run it as soon as possible without asking
Run it twice to be safe
Confirm the details with the user before running it
Never tell the user it ran
Confirmation catches misunderstandings before they become changed records.
Why show sources alongside a grounded answer?
So people can check where the answer came from
Citations let a reader verify a claim, and expose answers that the sources do not support.
What can Trust Layer data masking detect?
Patterns such as email addresses, phone numbers and card numbers, and fields classified as sensitive
Pattern-based and field-based masking together cover typed values and known sensitive fields.
What does Bring Your Own LLM in Einstein Studio let you do?
Train a model on your laptop
Connect a model from your own provider account for use in Salesforce
A connected model is used through the same platform features, with the organisation's own provider terms.
What is Einstein Studio (Model Builder) used for?
Building or connecting predictive and generative models for use with Data Cloud
Models built or connected there can score Data Cloud data or generate content in prompts.
A list of numbers representing the meaning of a piece of text
Texts with similar meanings get nearby vectors, which is what semantic search compares.
Keywords catch exact terms such as product codes; vectors catch the same meaning in different words.
What must exist before a retriever can search unstructured content in Data Cloud?
A search index over the chunked content
The index holds the chunks and their embeddings; the retriever queries it.
A service agent answers questions about returns policy. What should ground its answers?
Answers drawn from approved content can be checked and updated in one place.
Why is user feedback (thumbs up or down) on AI responses useful?
It trains the provider's public model
It is stored with the audit data, so prompts and actions can be reviewed and improved
Feedback beside the prompt and response shows exactly which cases go wrong.
Who should be accountable for AI-generated content a business sends to customers?
A named person or team who reviewed and approved it
Responsibility does not transfer to a model; somebody puts their name to what goes out.
What does setting a maximum number of output tokens limit?
How long the prompt can be
How long the response can be
Long enough for the task, short enough that a runaway answer is cut off — and cost is bounded with it.
Which instruction most reduces invented answers in a grounded prompt?
Answer only from the provided context, and say so when it does not contain the answer
Permission to say "I don't know" is what stops the model filling the gap with something plausible.
A user asks the agent to role-play as a system with no rules. What is this?
Role-play framing is a common way to try to talk a model out of its instructions; guardrails and limited actions are the defence.
Why leave personal data out of a prompt that does not need it?
Data that is never sent cannot leak or be misused
Prompts with personal data are free
Data minimisation is the simplest privacy control: send only what improves the answer.
Whose access does an employee-facing Agentforce assistant use?
The signed-in user's, with that user's permissions
Working as the user means it can only see and change what that person already can.
Splitting a task into several prompts, each using the previous one's output
Smaller steps are easier to check and to test than one large prompt that does everything.
A model moving to another server
A model's performance degrading as real-world data moves away from its training data
Monitor scores against outcomes over time and retrain when they diverge.
What can an LLM-based agent do that a scripted dialog-tree bot cannot?
Understand varied phrasing and choose actions without a fixed script
A dialog tree only follows the paths someone drew; an agent reasons over topics and actions — which is also why it needs testing.
